title: Hardware Accelerators and Optimization Algorithms for Unconventional Computing | EECS at UC Berkeley
content: Hardware Accelerators and Optimization Algorithms for Unconventional Computing | EECS at UC Berkeley Hardware Accelerators and Optimization Algorithms for Unconventional Computing Philip Canoza EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2023-3 January 13, 2023 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2023/EECS-2023-3.pdf Ising machines have emerged as a new paradigm in unconventional computing that can solve NP-Hard problems. This report looks at both the hardware and algorithm design of these Ising machines. First we will take a look at the implementations of two different hardware accelerators. The first accelerator is a digitally-synthesized, Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) that performs synchronous Gibbs sampling of a Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM). The second accelerator is an asynchronous neural network that uses a mixed-analog signal neuron to drive stochastic local updates. On the algorithmic side, we explore mappings of the Travelling Salesman Problem. In particular, we introduce a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) mapping that uses the classical k-opt algorithm to perform local search.
